Paragraph:
Translation: Now all of you must give full support to Grandfather Bhisma, standing at your respective strategic points in the phalanx of the army.

Purport (Excerpt): Duryodhana, after praising the prowess of Bhisma, further considered that others might think that they had been considered less important, so in his usual diplomatic way, he tried to adjust the situation... He emphasized that Bhismadeva was undoubtedly the greatest hero, but he was an old man, so everyone must especially think of his protection... Duryodhana clearly felt that the victory of the Kurus depended on the presence of Bhismadeva.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Realizing that his intense praise for Bhisma might have alienated or demoralized his other generals, Duryodhana attempts to walk back his earlier statements and diplomatically appease everyone by giving them the task of 'protecting' Bhisma.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Duryodhana uses manipulation and flattery to manage the fragile egos of his commanders. He disguises his own reliance on Bhisma by framing Bhisma as an older man who needs the collective protection of the others.
Outcome/Resolution: He temporarily patches up potential infighting, but his words are built on anxiety and diplomatic maneuvering rather than genuine leadership.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Kapatya (Deceit or diplomatic hypocrisy to mask inner insecurity)
Chinta (Anxiety driving constant recalibration of external situations)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The text highlights the restless, exhausting nature of leadership rooted in ego and adharma. Duryodhana must constantly manipulate his alliances and flatter his subordinates because his army is held together by material interests and mutual guilt rather than a unifying spiritual truth.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Duryodhana exhibits the behavior of an anxious micromanager trying to perform damage control. Aware he committed a social faux pas by over-praising one individual, he awkwardly pivots to make everyone feel essential, revealing how a leader lacking internal stability constantly reacts out of fear of losing control.
